'''Awvee Storey''' (born April 18, 1977) is a former American professional [[basketball]] player and assistant coach for the [[Connecticut Sun]] of the [[WNBA]]. He played the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions.

==High school career==
Born in [[Chicago, Illinois]], Storey formed a relationship with Bennet Wang who ran an inner-city basketball league. Storey's mother relinquished Storey into Bennet Wang's care.<ref>[http://proteinwisdom.com/?p=9662 Bennet Wang] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302184438/http://proteinwisdom.com/?p=9662|date=March 2, 2016}}. protein wisdom (August 26, 2007). Retrieved on 2016-04-29.</ref> Storey attended [[Proviso West High School]] in [[Hillside, Illinois]], in 1996–97, he played for New Hampton Prep.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Player Bio: Awvee Storey |url=https://thesundevils.com/sports/2013/4/17/208247419.aspx |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Arizona State University Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Storey played his freshman season at the [[University of Illinois]] before transferring to [[Arizona State University]], sitting out the 1998–99 season.

Storey was one of the top rebounders in the [[Pacific-10 Conference|Pac-10]], at only 6–6. He made an immediate impact and gave the young squad some veteran leadership despite being only a sophomore. Blessed with excellent athletic ability, Storey was able to defend guards, forwards and, when necessary, a center. He posted 16 double-doubles in his 85-game career. In 2000–01, he earned Pac-10 Honorable Mention honours, after posting career-highs in points (13.1) and rebounds (9.1), the latter a conference best.

Storey earned his bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies degree with concentrations in communications and sociology at ASU. In the summer of 2001, he worked for [[Fox Sports Arizona]] as a production department intern.

==NBA career==
Awvee played in the NBA from 2004 to 2008. He played with the [[New Jersey Nets]] from 2004 to 2005, the [[Washington Wizards]] from 2005 to 2006, and the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] from 2007 to 2008.

Storey's final NBA game ever was played on April 16, 2008, in a 101–110 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] where he recorded 7 points, 4 rebounds and 1 assist. Coincidentally, Timberwolves' forward [[Kirk Snyder]] also played his final NBA game during this matchup, recording 6 points, 3 rebounds and 2 assists.

On December 21, 2006, as a member of the [[NBA Development League]]'s [[Dakota Wizards]], [[Martynas Andriuškevičius]] sustained a serious head injury when he was punched by teammate Awvee Storey in an altercation during practice in [[Bismarck, North Dakota]]. The center suffered a [[fractured skull]], severe [[concussion]], and a two-centimeter [[hematoma]] (bruise) on the left side of his [[brain]]. Doctors initially thought it would be months before he could speak, but he was able to within a month, and stated his desire to play basketball within a year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailyherald.com/sports/story.asp?id%3D265275 |accessdate=November 5, 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207162534/http://www.dailyherald.com/sports/story.asp?id=265275 |archivedate=February 7, 2012 |title=Chicago Bears|work=Daily Herald}}</ref> Storey was suspended indefinitely.<ref name=fight>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2707338 One player suspended, another hospitalized after fight]. Sports.espn.go.com (December 25, 2006). Retrieved on 2016-04-29.</ref><ref name=recovery>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2717155 Andriuskevicius recovering slowly after fight]. Sports.espn.go.com (January 3, 2007). Retrieved on 2016-04-29.</ref> Days later he had his contract terminated and he was dismissed from the league.<ref name=dismissed>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2721312 NBDL player Storey dismissed for punching teammate]. Sports.espn.go.com (January 5, 2007). Retrieved on 2016-04-29.</ref> Andriuškevičius did not wish to pursue charges.<ref name=fight/><ref name=recovery/><ref name=dismissed/>

== Coaching career ==
In 2010–11, Storey was a video coordinator for the Washington Wizards. He joined the [[Washington Mystics]] in 2011. His task at the Mystics included assisting with scouting, workouts, and player development. After a seven-year stint with the team, he joined the [[Chicago Sky]] as an assistant coach in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-11 |title=Chicago Sky Hire Former NBA Player Awvee Storey as Assistant Coach |url=https://sky.wnba.com/news/chicago-sky-name-awvee-storey-assistant-coach/ |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Chicago Sky |language=en}}</ref> Storey worked as an assistant to head coach [[Jarell Christian]] with the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]] in the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Capital City Go-Go |url=https://www.nba.com/resources/static/team/v2/lakers/media/2018-19-South-Bay-Lakers-Media-Guide.pdf |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=2018-19 South Bay Lakers Media Guide}}</ref> On May 19, 2019, Storey was appointed as a video coordinator of WNBA's [[Connecticut Sun]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sun Announce Hiring Of Awvee Storey |url=https://sun.wnba.com/news/sun-announce-hiring-of-awvee-storey/ |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Connecticut Sun |language=en}}</ref> He helped guide the team to the 2019 WNBA Finals and took over the role as the Sun's player development coach on January 3, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Storey returns to Sun staff as Player Development Coach |url=https://sun.wnba.com/news/storey-returns-to-sun-staff-as-player-development-coach/ |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Connecticut Sun |language=en}}</ref> In the 2021–22 season, he served as an assistant coach for the [[Maine Celtics]] of the NBA G League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deng Adel and Charles Cooke III of the Maine Celtics review game tape... |url=https://www.gettyimages.ca/detail/news-photo/deng-adel-and-charles-cooke-iii-of-the-maine-celtics-review-news-photo/1238863399 |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Getty Images |date=March 2, 2022 |language=}}</ref>
